statement: Sketch the graph of $y=\dfrac{x}{x^{2}+1}$, stating any symmetries, intercepts and turning points.
solution:
Since $f(-x)=-f(x)$, the curve is odd (symmetric about the origin). It passes through the origin $(0,0)$.
Differentiating,
$$y'=\frac{(x^{2}+1)-x(2x)}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}=\frac{1-x^{2}}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}.$$
Stationary points occur at $x=\pm1$. At $x=1$, $y=\tfrac12$; at $x=-1$, $y=-\tfrac12$. Since $y'$ changes from positive to negative at $x=1$, $(1,\tfrac12)$ is a maximum; $(-1,-\tfrac12)$ is a minimum.
As $x\to\pm\infty$, $y\to0$, so the $x$-axis is an asymptote.
hints: Examine the sign of $y'$ near $x=\pm1$ and as $x\to\infty$.
